pharm: Dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor; enhances incretin (GLP-1, GIP) activity to improve glucose-dependent insulin secretion and lower glucagon
quick: 50 mg once or twice daily PO; max 100 mg/day
Take with or without food, same times daily
Avoid - safety not established (Pending review: not FDA-approved)
Avoid; not known if excreted in human milk
Reduce to 50 mg once daily in moderate/severe impairment
Limit; excess may impair glucose control and liver
LFTs at baseline then periodically, HbA1c, glucose
summary: Vildagliptin (brand Galvus) is an EMA-approved oral DPP-4 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes mellitus, used as monotherapy or combined with metformin, a sulfonylurea, a thiazolidinedione, or insulin. It blocks degradation of incretin hormones, increasing glucose-dependent insulin release and suppressing glucagon, with low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk. Liver enzyme monitoring is required because of rare hepatic dysfunction. It is not FDA-approved; this record is pending clinical review.
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus as monotherapy when diet and exercise alone are inadequate and metformin is inappropriate due to intolerance/contraindication
Type 2 diabetes as dual oral therapy with metformin, a sulfonylurea, or a thiazolidinedione when glycaemic control is inadequate
Type 2 diabetes as triple oral therapy with a sulfonylurea and metformin
Type 2 diabetes in combination with insulin (with or without metformin) when diet, exercise and stable insulin do not provide adequate control

dosage.c: Type 2 diabetes - monotherapy or with metformin or thiazolidinedione
dosage.d: 50 mg twice daily (100 mg/day total), one dose in the morning and one in the evening
dosage.t: Morning and evening, with or without food
dosage.n: Maximum recommended daily dose is 100 mg

dosage.c: Type 2 diabetes - combination with a sulfonylurea
dosage.d: 50 mg once daily in the morning
dosage.n: Doses above 50 mg once daily with a sulfonylurea give no added benefit and increase hypoglycaemia risk; consider lower sulfonylurea dose

dosage.c: Type 2 diabetes - combination with insulin (with/without metformin)
dosage.n: Monitor for hypoglycaemia; insulin dose may need reduction

dosage.c: Moderate or severe renal impairment / end-stage renal disease
dosage.n: Dose reduction required when eGFR <50 mL/min; no adjustment needed in mild impairment

admin: Swallow tablets whole; may be taken with or without food
When dosed twice daily, give one dose in the morning and one in the evening
When combined with a sulfonylurea, give the single 50 mg dose in the morning
Obtain liver function tests before starting and at intervals thereafter
Do not initiate if ALT or AST exceeds 3 times the upper limit of normal
moa: Vildagliptin is a potent, selective, reversible inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4), the enzyme that rapidly inactivates the incretin hormones glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP). By inhibiting DPP-4 it increases endogenous incretin levels, which enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells and suppresses inappropriate glucagon secretion from alpha cells. The net effect is improved fasting and postprandial glycaemic control with a low intrinsic risk of hypoglycaemia because the insulinotropic action is glucose-dependent.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to vildagliptin or any excipient
Hepatic impairment, including pre-treatment ALT or AST greater than 3 times the upper limit of normal
relative: Severe congestive heart failure (NYHA class IV - limited experience)
Concomitant sulfonylurea or insulin (increased hypoglycaemia risk)
Severe renal impairment / ESRD (dose reduction and caution)

preg: Pending clinical review - not FDA-approved. There are no adequate data in pregnant women; avoid use during pregnancy. Insulin is the preferred treatment for diabetes during pregnancy. EMA SmPC advises that vildagliptin should not be used in pregnancy.
lact: It is not known whether vildagliptin is excreted in human milk; animal studies show excretion into milk. Use during breastfeeding is not recommended.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed in mild renal impairment (eGFR >=50 mL/min). In moderate or severe renal impairment and in end-stage renal disease (including dialysis), reduce the dose to 50 mg once daily.
hepatic: Contraindicated in hepatic impairment. Do not start if baseline ALT or AST is greater than 3 times the upper limit of normal. Rare cases of hepatic dysfunction (including hepatitis) have been reported; monitor liver enzymes and discontinue if persistent transaminase elevation, jaundice, or other signs of liver injury occur.

major: Sulfonylureas (e.g., glimepiride, gliclazide) - increased risk of hypoglycaemia; consider reducing sulfonylurea dose
moderate: ACE inhibitors - possible increased risk of angioedema
Drugs that may impair glucose tolerance (corticosteroids, thiazides, sympathomimetics) may reduce glycaemic control
minor: Low potential for cytochrome P450-mediated interactions; vildagliptin is not a significant CYP substrate, inhibitor, or inducer
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food does not clinically affect absorption
interactions.alcohol: Excessive alcohol can impair glycaemic control and may add to hepatic risk; advise moderation
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor liver enzymes as transaminase elevations can occur; no specific assay interference established

common: Hypoglycaemia (when combined with sulfonylurea or insulin)
emergency: Severe hypoglycaemia - treat with oral or IV glucose
Angioedema with airway compromise - stop drug and give emergency airway/anaphylaxis management
Acute pancreatitis with severe persistent abdominal pain - discontinue and evaluate urgently

monitoring: Liver function tests (ALT, AST) before initiation, every 3 months during the first year, and periodically thereafter
Signs and symptoms of pancreatitis (persistent severe abdominal pain)
Signs of hypoglycaemia when used with a sulfonylurea or insulin
Skin lesions and signs of angioedema
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food
Report yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent nausea, fatigue, or right upper abdominal pain (possible liver problem)
Seek urgent care for severe, persistent abdominal pain that may radiate to the back (possible pancreatitis)
Stop the drug and seek help for swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat or difficulty breathing
Learn to recognise and treat low blood sugar, especially if also taking a sulfonylurea or insulin
Continue diet, exercise, and regular blood glucose and liver monitoring as advised
pk: Rapid DPP-4 inhibition; >90% enzyme inhibition within ~45 minutes of dosing
Plasma peak (Tmax) about 1.7 hours when fasting; bioavailability ~85%
DPP-4 inhibition sustained over the dosing interval supporting once- or twice-daily dosing
Store below 30 degrees C in the original blister, protected from moisture
pearls: Pending clinical review - not FDA-approved; EMA-approved (Galvus) and widely used in Europe and Asia
Liver enzymes must be checked at baseline and periodically; contraindicated if ALT/AST >3x ULN or in hepatic impairment
Low intrinsic hypoglycaemia risk as monotherapy; hypoglycaemia mainly arises when combined with sulfonylurea or insulin
Use 50 mg once daily with a sulfonylurea and in moderate/severe renal impairment
Weight-neutral and does not require routine cardiac monitoring, but use caution in severe heart failure
Consider pancreatitis and angioedema (especially with ACE inhibitors) as class effects of gliptins
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Vildagliptin is generally well tolerated; reported high doses have caused muscle pain, mild and transient paraesthesia, fever, oedema, and a transient rise in lipase. There is no specific antidote. Vildagliptin is not removed by haemodialysis, although the major hydrolysis metabolite can be. Management is supportive with removal of unabsorbed drug, clinical monitoring (including liver enzymes), and correction of any hypoglycaemia with glucose.
